kpis.change: $27.1bn, ~10.2% guided FY26 growth incl. ~$480m acquired Semrush ARR

sections.title: Growth, Margins & Cash Generation
sections.subtitle: The core software economics: durable growth, high and stable margins, and the SBC gap between reported and owner cash flow

charts.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF (after SBC)
charts.annotation: Owner FCF is Reported FCF less SBC (and, in the DCF, cash taxes on equity-award net-share settlement) -- the TTM figures ($10,280m reported vs $7,833m owner, a 9.71%-of-revenue SBC drag) live in the DCF JSON, not this CSV, and anchor the Owner FCF KPI card above. This chart shows the two disclosed CSV inputs to that gap.

charts.title: Stock-Based Comp as % of Revenue
charts.annotation: TTM basis in the DCF (9.71%, including cash taxes on equity-award settlement) runs slightly lower than the raw CSV SBC-only ratio shown here, and is declining -- the opposite of the usual SaaS dilution warning.

sections.title: Subscription Base & ARR
sections.subtitle: ARR was redefined in FY2026 -- the two series below are never the same line

charts.title: ARR: Digital Media (legacy) vs Total Adobe (current)
charts.annotation: Digital Media ARR ($19.20bn FY2025) is the metric Adobe reported through FY2025. Total Adobe ARR ($25.20bn FY2025, $27.10bn Q2-FY2026) is the broader FY2026 replacement, disclosed alongside Digital Media ARR only at the FY2024/FY2025 bridge points. Chaining them (19.2 -> 26.06) would fabricate ~36% growth; the company's own reported growth is ~10-11%.

charts.title: Segment Revenue (through FY2025)
charts.annotation: Adobe moved to a single reportable segment from FY2026 (Semrush folded into Digital Experience through Q1, then unified) -- the series stops at FY2025 because the company itself stopped disclosing the split, not because either business shrank.

charts.title: Subscription Revenue vs Total Revenue
charts.annotation: Subscription has been ~96-97% of total revenue for the full disclosed history -- the gap between the two lines is the small, structurally declining non-subscription (publishing/advertising) tail.

sections.title: Capital Structure & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: Buyback-funded share count decline against a modest net-debt position

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: 485.5m (FY2020) -> 402.5m (Q2-FY2026), a 17% reduction, funded by $11.28bn of FY2025 repurchases against $50bn of authorizations running to 2028/2030 on a ~$116bn market cap. The DCF holds the count flat going forward rather than projecting further reduction, since SBC dilution is already fully expensed in the flows.

charts.title: Cash & Equivalents vs Total Debt
charts.annotation: Net debt was $1,726m as of Q2-FY2026 (debt exceeds cash) -- modest for the scale of cash generation, and small enough that interest income is left in the DCF's flows rather than stripped out.

charts.title: Net Income vs Reported FCF
charts.annotation: FCF has run consistently above net income for a decade -- D&A and working-capital timing exceed the (real, but non-cash) SBC charge sitting inside net income. See the Reported vs Owner FCF chart for the cash cost SBC represents once it is added back out.

revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Total reported revenue and its year-over-year growth rate.

For Adobe: Revenue has compounded at a 10.5% 3-year / 13.1% 5-year CAGR through a subscription base that is ~96-97% recurring. FY2026 guidance was raised twice this year to $26.50-26.60bn (~12% YoY), including Semrush revenue from its April 2026 close.

What to watch:

  • Whether growth holds in the high single/low double digits as freemium conversion and Firefly monetization scale against AI-native substitution
  • Q3 FY2026 results (mid-September 2026) -- management has pre-warned net-new Digital Media ARR will look soft by design

margins.title: Gross & Operating Margin
margins.content:
Gross margin (revenue less cost of revenue) and operating margin (after opex), both as a % of revenue.

For Adobe: Gross margin has held near 87-89% for a decade -- typical of mature enterprise software with low delivery cost. Operating margin sits around 33-37%, dipping to 17.5% in Q1 FY2024 on a one-off Figma break fee.

What to watch:

  • Whether Firefly's compute cost (a genuine COGS item, unlike prior software margins) begins to compress gross margin as AI usage scales
  • Opex discipline as Adobe absorbs Semrush and funds the freemium acquisition push

fcfGap.title: Reported FCF vs Owner FCF (after SBC)
fcfGap.content:
Reported free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex) versus stock-based compensation, the two disclosed inputs to the owner-FCF adjustment used in the DCF.

For Adobe: TTM reported FCF is $10,280m (40.8% margin) but SBC plus cash taxes paid on equity-award net-share settlement is $2,447m (9.71% of revenue), leaving owner FCF of $7,833m (30.9% margin) -- the actual per-share cash generation once the real cost of equity compensation is charged. This 24% haircut is the single largest judgment call in the valuation.

What to watch:

  • SBC as a % of revenue continuing its multi-year decline (12.4% in FY2020 to 9.7% TTM) rather than reversing
  • Whether reported FCF growth and owner FCF growth stay in step (they have: 10.99% vs 10.03% 3-year CAGR) -- a widening gap would mean dilution is outrunning cash generation

sbcPct.title: Stock-Based Comp as % of Revenue
sbcPct.content:
SBC expense (cash-flow-statement add-back) as a percentage of revenue -- the raw dilution-funding rate before the DCF's further addition of cash taxes on equity-award settlement.

For Adobe: This ratio has fallen for several consecutive years even as revenue and headcount for AI initiatives have grown, which is why owner-FCF CAGR (10.99%/14.87% 3yr/5yr) runs slightly ABOVE reported-FCF CAGR (10.03%/13.17%) -- the usual SaaS warning sign (SBC growing faster than revenue) is not present here.

What to watch:

  • Any reversal as Adobe competes for AI/ML talent against well-funded startups and hyperscalers
  • The DCF's projected path continues the decline from 9.6% to 8.0% by year 10 -- a stall above that path would compress owner FCF versus the base case

arr.title: ARR: Digital Media (legacy) vs Total Adobe (current)
arr.content:
Annual Recurring Run-Rate, Adobe's primary operating KPI, converting current subscription bookings into an annualized figure. FY2026 introduced a broader definition (Total Adobe ARR) that supersedes the legacy Digital Media ARR series.

For Adobe: Digital Media ARR reached $19.20bn at FY2025 under the old definition. Total Adobe ARR -- disclosed alongside it at the FY2024/FY2025 bridge -- was $22.61bn (FY2024) and $25.20bn (FY2025), reaching $27.10bn by Q2-FY2026 (including ~$480m of acquired Semrush ARR). These are two different rulers: chaining the legacy series into the new one would imply ~36% one-year growth that never happened. True FY2026 guided growth is ~10.2%.

What to watch:

  • Organic growth (excluding the Semrush acquisition) trending below the historical >10% level as freemium conversion and deferred price increases work through the base
  • Q3 FY2026 net-new ARR (due mid-September 2026), which management has told investors to expect will look soft by design before reaccelerating

segment.title: Segment Revenue (through FY2025)
segment.content:
Adobe's two historical reportable segments: Digital Media (Creative Cloud + Document Cloud) and Digital Experience (Experience Cloud, now including Semrush).

For Adobe: Digital Media has grown from $9.2bn (FY2020) to $17.6bn (FY2025), ~74% of revenue; Digital Experience from $3.1bn to $5.9bn. Adobe moved to a single reportable segment starting FY2026, so this chart's series necessarily end at FY2025 -- that is a disclosure change, not a business contraction.

What to watch:

  • Whether qualitative commentary on Digital Media vs Digital Experience (still given in earnings calls even without the segment table) shows either business decelerating

subscriptionMix.title: Subscription Revenue vs Total Revenue
subscriptionMix.content:
Revenue billed as recurring subscriptions versus Adobe's total reported revenue.

For Adobe: Subscription has been a stable ~96-97% of total revenue for the entire disclosed history -- among the highest recurring-revenue mixes of any large-cap software company, which is the basis for using an owner-FCF DCF rather than a multiple-only approach.

What to watch:

  • The small non-subscription tail (perpetual licenses, publishing, advertising) continuing its structural decline -- it is a rounding error on growth but not on mix quality

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Fully diluted shares outstanding at each period end.

For Adobe: Down from 485.5m (FY2020) to 402.5m (Q2-FY2026), a 17% reduction driven by $11.28bn of FY2025 repurchases and $4.59bn in H1-FY2026, against $50bn of authorizations running to 2028/2030 -- large relative to the ~$116bn market cap. This is genuinely funded by ~$10bn+/year of cash generation, not a modelling convention.

What to watch:

  • Whether buyback pace holds as Adobe also funds the Semrush acquisition and continued AI infrastructure investment
  • The DCF holds the count flat for the 10-year projection rather than assuming further reduction, since SBC is already fully expensed in the flows and charging both would double-count

debtCash.title: Cash & Equivalents vs Total Debt
debtCash.content:
Balance-sheet cash and equivalents against total debt outstanding.

For Adobe: Q2-FY2026 shows $4,919m cash against $6,645m debt -- a modest $1,726m net debt position, small for the scale of cash generation ($10bn+ annual reported FCF). Debt rose from ~$4.1bn (pre-2024) to ~$5.6-6.6bn as Adobe funded the Semrush acquisition and buybacks.

What to watch:

  • Whether net debt continues to creep up as further M&A and buybacks are funded partly by borrowing rather than cash alone
  • The DCF leaves interest income in the flows (rather than stripping it) because Adobe carries net debt, not net cash

niVsFcf.title: Net Income vs Reported FCF
niVsFcf.content:
GAAP net income against reported free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex).

For Adobe: FCF has exceeded net income in every full fiscal year shown, reflecting D&A and working-capital timing (deferred revenue inflows from annual subscription billing) running ahead of the SBC expense embedded in net income. FY2025 reported FCF was $9,852m against net income of $7,130m.

What to watch:

  • This gap overstates true owner economics because SBC is a real (if non-cash) cost of running the business -- see the Reported vs Owner FCF chart for the adjustment the DCF actually uses

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (5.5%), building to a 10-year path averaging below the 10.99% 3-year owner-FCF CAGR
